beats.subline: Wednesday, November 18, 2026 close — a choppy, mixed session as Nvidia's post-earnings pop faded while traders braced for Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut.
beats.body: Nvidia gave back part of its post-earnings gain and UnitedHealth led healthcare stocks lower, pulling the Dow down for a second straight day, while the Nasdaq managed a small gain; Anthropic priced its IPO above its $70-$78 range after the close, setting up Thursday's record Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT.

beats.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen, but no nuclear arms deal emerges
beats.body: The three leaders met on the sidelines of the APEC summit for an unprecedented three-way sit-down focused on nuclear arms reduction, along with the Iran war and Ukraine, and issued a joint declaration; Russia and China showed little appetite for binding new limits on their arsenals, and no reduction agreement was confirmed, with Xi saying he favors prohibiting nuclear weapons but declining to call the talks an arms-control effort.

beats.headline: US tightens AI-chip export curbs to close China's cloud loophole; Beijing warns of countermeasures
beats.body: A new Commerce Department rule adds license requirements for advanced AI-chip exports to overseas data centers that Chinese firms could use to access the chips remotely, targeting diversion through countries including Singapore, Malaysia and Brazil, and formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule; China's Commerce Ministry called the move unjustified and warned it would take countermeasures to protect its sovereignty and security interests.

beats.headline: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut opens 34% above its IPO price in the largest-ever public offering
beats.body: Shares of Claude's maker began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT at $111.50, about 34% above the $83 IPO price, after the $81.3 billion offering set a record as the largest IPO in history; the stock pulled back toward the $100-$101 range by midday as broader markets, including the Dow, fell more than 600 points amid profit-taking in AI names.
